useCase.title: 24/7 Voice AI for Customer Service
useCase.description: Many small businesses get a large share of calls after hours. Missed calls become voicemails or lost leads; a full call center is out of reach. We built a voice AI that answers every call, looks up answers from the client’s knowledge base, and escalates to a human or CRM when needed. LangChain runs the pipeline: one agent with tools for retrieval and handoff, so we didn’t wire up separate scripts per intent.
capabilities: Answer inbound calls 24/7 instead of sending to voicemail
Answer FAQs (hours, locations, pricing) from the business’s own docs
Escalate to a human or create a CRM ticket when the caller asks or the agent is unsure
Keep conversation context so callers can ask follow-ups without repeating
Log transcripts and outcomes for compliance and improving prompts
queries: How does the voice AI know what to say?
What happens when the AI doesn’t know the answer?
How do you connect the voice AI to our existing knowledge base?
What’s the implementation timeline for 24/7 coverage?
metrics: Share of after-hours calls handled without human (tracked per client)
Escalation rate and main escalation reasons
Cost per handled call vs. outsourced or in-house alternatives
Time to first response and call duration (for tuning)

architecture.description: Inbound call hits a telephony gateway (e.g. Retell or Twilio). Audio is streamed to speech-to-text; transcript is sent to a LangChain agent. The agent has tools: search the knowledge base (e.g. Weaviate or another vector store), lookup CRM, and escalate. It chooses the tool, gets the result, and replies in natural language. Response is turned back into speech and streamed to the caller. Session and turn history live in LangChain memory so follow-up questions work.

components.name: Voice gateway and STT/TTS
components.description: Telephony ingress plus speech-to-text and text-to-speech so the rest of the stack works on text.
components.details: Handles SIP or provider API, buffering, and streaming. STT and TTS can be swapped (e.g. Whisper, provider APIs) without changing the agent.
explanation: Single place where voice becomes text and text becomes voice
Latency and cost depend on the provider

components.name: LangChain conversation agent
components.description: One agent that decides what to do next: answer from context, call a tool, or escalate.
components.details: Single LLM (e.g. GPT-4 or Claude) with a fixed set of tools: search_knowledge_base, get_customer_record, create_ticket, escalate_to_human. Prompt defines persona, guardrails, and when to hand off.
explanation: One orchestration layer instead of separate scripts per intent
Tool results go back into the same conversation so the agent can refine the answer

components.name: Knowledge-base retriever
components.description: Semantic search over the business’s docs (PDFs, help articles, FAQs) so answers are grounded in their content.
components.details: Documents are chunked, embedded, and stored in a vector DB. The LangChain tool queries it and returns the top-k chunks; the agent cites or paraphrases them.
explanation: Ties answers to real content and reduces hallucination
Updating content updates answers without retraining

components.name: Session and conversation memory
components.description: Stores turn-by-turn history and optional summary so the agent has full context for the rest of the call.
components.details: LangChain memory (e.g. buffer or windowed) is keyed by call/session ID. Optionally persist a short summary to CRM after the call.
explanation: Callers don’t have to repeat themselves on follow-up questions
Escalations can include a short summary for the human agent

flow.description: Telephony gateway receives the call and opens a stream to STT and the agent.
flow.details: Provider-specific (e.g. Retell, Twilio). Agent process is invoked with a new session ID.

flow.description: Streaming audio is transcribed in real time; partial or final transcript is sent to the agent.
flow.details: Latency vs. accuracy is configurable; typically a few hundred ms per utterance.

flow.description: LangChain agent receives the user message, may call tools (KB search, CRM, escalate), then produces a text reply.
flow.details: Tools are called as needed; reply is conditioned on tool results and conversation history.

flow.description: Agent’s reply is sent to TTS and streamed back to the caller.
flow.details: Voice and tone can be tuned via TTS model or provider settings.

flow.description: Transcript, tool calls, and outcome (resolved vs. escalated) are logged; optional CRM ticket or contact update.
flow.details: Used for compliance, analytics, and prompt or model tuning.

requirements: Knowledge base (docs, FAQs) or a plan to build one
Telephony provider account (e.g. Retell, Twilio) and phone number
CRM API access if you want lookup or ticket creation
Staging environment to test prompts and tools before go-live
success_metrics: Cost per call and time to first response
integration_points: Vector store or search (Weaviate, Pinecone, or existing search)
